subject: sociology
title: Gender at Work Adventure
welcome_lead: Different jobs, different pay — what's the gender story? 💼
meta_desc: Gender Roles Adventure 2 — KS3 Sociology on gender, jobs and pay.
final_note: You learned about the gender pay gap and progress for women at work.

walkthroughs.body_html:
UK women earn around ~14% less than men on average for full-time work.

Reasons include time off for childcare, fewer in top jobs, and historic bias.

The glass ceiling = invisible barrier stopping women reaching top jobs.

Only a small share of UK CEOs are women — though growing slowly.

The Equality Act 2010 bans gender discrimination at work.

More girls now study STEM.

More men take paternity leave.

Roles are shifting — slowly. 🛠️

mcqs.q: What is the postmodern view of identity?
options: Everyone has the same identity in postmodern society.
Identity is fixed by class, gender, and ethnicity at birth.
Identities are fluid, fragmented, and constructed through consumption and choice.

mcqs.q: What is Merton's strain theory of crime?
options: Strain theory says people commit crime because they are stressed.
Strain theory says criminals have psychological strain disorders.

Crime results from a mismatch between cultural goals (success, wealth) and legitimate means of achieving them — those who can't access legitimate means may innovate (crime), ritualise, retreat or rebel.
